headline: Jefferies strategist Chris Wood warned that the debt-funded AI spending of America's big tech companies may not earn enough to justify it, which would destroy a great deal of capital.
score_reason: Pool score 6 lowered by 1: the quoted views come from a 17 Sep interview and the 9 Oct Bloomberg story could not be read.
importance_line: Savers and pension holders with stock exposure, and lenders to AI builders, are the people whose money is at stake, but this is one strategist's base case with no timetable.
summary: TokenPost reports that Chris Wood, global head of equity strategy at the investment bank Jefferies, said in an interview on 17 Sep that his base case is that hyperscalers (the biggest cloud-computing companies) will not earn returns that justify their AI investment, which is increasingly financed by debt rather than cash. Bloomberg carried a story under the headline "Massive Capital Destruction" on 9 Oct; Wood gave no timetable and said the AI trade could unravel if credit markets withdraw funding.
notes: Bloomberg original blocked; facts from TokenPost. Our 3 Oct 2026 edition carried a different Wood item (bond yields). No investment advice.
